title: Special Consumer Rules
summary: These passages outline the Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020, which came into force on July 20, 2020 under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. They define the setup and administrative support for Mediation Cells established at District, State, and National Commissions. The rules explicitly bar certain matters from mediation, such as cases of serious fraud, severe medical negligence, and criminal offences, while giving Commissions discretion to withhold references. Additionally, they cover provisions for application fee refunds upon settlement, prohibitions against parallel legal proceedings, and the continuation of settlement agreements after a party's death.
key_points: The Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020 came into force on July 20, 2020.
Mediation Cells are established within Commissions and maintain a panel of mediators recommended by a selection committee.
Matters involving grievous medical negligence, fraud, non-compoundable offences, or broad public interest cannot be referred to mediation.
Commissions may decline to refer a matter to mediation if no acceptable elements of settlement exist.
Complainants receive a full refund of application fees if a settlement is successfully reached through mediation.
Parties under active mediation are prohibited from initiating arbitral or judicial proceedings on the same matter.
A settlement agreement is not discharged by the death of a party and is enforceable by or against legal representatives.

important_provisions.description: Establishes the title of the rules and sets their commencement date as July 20, 2020.
Provides for the creation of Mediation Cells, mediator panels, support staff, and government assistance.
Enumerates categories of cases excluded from mediation and gives the Commission discretion to decline reference.
Entitles the complainant to a full refund of application fees if a settlement is achieved.
Bars parties from initiating arbitral or judicial proceedings regarding matters subject to mediation.
Ensures settlement agreements are not discharged by a party's death and remain enforceable by or against legal representatives.
